description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 2 on t/op/lex.t:211).

perl: an `@` inside an interpolating string is a literal `@` unless what
follows can START an identifier.  A DIGIT never can -- fullwidth or not.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, probes/p4.pl):

    my $r = eval "qq'\@\x{ff13}'";
    printf "eval=[%s] err=[%s]\n", (defined $r ? $r : 'UNDEF'), $@;
    my $q = qq'@\x{ff13}';
    printf "qq=[%s]\n", $q;

    perl: eval=[@<U+FF13>] err=[]      qq=[@<U+FF13>]
    PCL:  eval=[UNDEF]                 qq=[@<U+FF13>]
          err=[The variable |@<U+FF13>| is unbound. at (eval 1) line 1.]

So the DIRECT spelling is right and the STRING EVAL path is not: the fragment
re-parse takes the fullwidth digit as an identifier character after `@` and
emits a reference to an array of that name, which is unbound at load.

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/lex.t 25 `"@<fullwidth digit>"
[perl #123963]`.

SHAPE: the identifier-START rule, not the identifier-CHARACTER rule.  The two
paths disagree, so the fix is to make the eval path ask the same predicate the
direct path asks (rule 11 -- find the direct path's reading of "can this start
an identifier" before adding one).  Neighbours to probe at the same time:
`@` before an ASCII digit, before a space, and at end of string.
subject: SILENT WRONG inside a STRING EVAL: `@` before a non-identifier-START character (a fullwidth digit) is read as an ARRAY NAME; the direct spelling is right
